text.en: All consonants used in the Ainu language also appear in Japanese ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--all-consonants-used-in-the-ainu-language-also⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語で用いられる子音はすべて日本語にも現れる ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--all-consonants-used-in-the-ainu-language-also⟧。

text.en: The inventory and number of consonants are identical across all dialects except for their positions of occurrence within words ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-inventory-and-number-of-consonants-are-identical⟧. Ainu is analyzed as having eleven consonant phonemes, /p, t, k, c, s, h, m, n, r, y, w/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--ainu-eleven-consonant-phonemes⟧, or twelve consonant phonemes including the glottal stop /ʔ/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--ainu-twelve-consonant-phonemes⟧. Excluding the glottal stop, Hokkaido Ainu has eleven consonant phonemes ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--hokkaido-eleven-consonants-refsing⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu dialects, twelve consonants including the glottal stop can occur as syllable onsets, alongside five vowels, while nine consonants can appear in coda position ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-dialects-there-are-five-vowels⟧. Southern Hokkaido Ainu has twelve consonant phonemes: /p/, /t/, /k/, /c/, /s/, /r/, /m/, /n/, /w/, /y/, /h/, and /ʔ/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--southern-hokkaido-ainu-has-12-consonant-phonemes-p⟧. For Saru Ainu, the consonant inventory is reported to consist of /p/, /t/, /c/, /k/, /m/, /n/, /s/, /y/, /w/, /h/, /ɾ/, and a phonetic glottal stop [ʔ] ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-consonant-inventory-of-saru-ainu-consists-of⟧. Sakhalin Ainu has twelve consonant phonemes including the glottal stop: /p, t, k, c, s, r, m, n, w, y, h, ʔ/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--sakhalin-twelve-consonant-phonemes⟧. Kuril Ainu has ten consonants: /p, t, k, c, s, m, n, h, r, ʔ/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--kuril-ainu-has-ten-consonants-p-t-k⟧. Ainu lacks a contrast between palatalized and non-palatalized consonants ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--ainu-lacks-a-contrast-between-palatalized-and-non⟧. The affricate /c/ varies freely among [tʃ], [ts], [dʒ], and [dz] ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-affricate-c-varies-freely-among-t-ts⟧. Kirikae proposes that the articulation point of the affricate *c* is somewhat further forward than the consonant of Japanese *chu*, but not as far forward as Japanese *tsu* ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-articulation-point-of-the-ainu-affricate-c⟧.
text.ja: 子音の種類と数は語中の出現位置を除いてどの方言でも同じである ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-inventory-and-number-of-consonants-are-identical⟧。アイヌ語の子音音素については、/p, t, k, c, s, h, m, n, r, y, w/ の11個とする見解と ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--ainu-eleven-consonant-phonemes⟧、声門閉鎖音 /ʔ/ を含めた12個とする見解が存在する ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--ainu-twelve-consonant-phonemes⟧。声門破裂音を除くと、北海道アイヌ語には11個の子音音素が存在する ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--hokkaido-eleven-consonants-refsing⟧。北海道アイヌ語諸方言においては、5母音のほかに、音節頭子音として声門閉鎖音を含めて12個、音節末子音として9個の子音が生起しうる ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-dialects-there-are-five-vowels⟧。南北海道アイヌ語には、/p/、/t/、/k/、/c/、/s/、/r/、/m/、/n/、/w/、/y/、/h/、/ʔ/ の12の子音音素がある ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--southern-hokkaido-ainu-has-12-consonant-phonemes-p⟧。沙流アイヌ語の子音目録は /p/、/t/、/c/、/k/、/m/、/n/、/s/、/y/、/w/、/h/、/ɾ/ および音声的な声門閉鎖音 [ʔ] からなると報告されている ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-consonant-inventory-of-saru-ainu-consists-of⟧。樺太アイヌ語には声門閉鎖音を含めて12個の子音音素が存在する ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--sakhalin-twelve-consonant-phonemes⟧。千島アイヌ語の子音は /p, t, k, c, s, m, n, h, r, ʔ/ の10個である ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--kuril-ainu-has-ten-consonants-p-t-k⟧。口蓋化音と非口蓋化音（拗音と直音）の対立は存在しない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--ainu-lacks-a-contrast-between-palatalized-and-non⟧。破擦音 /c/ は [tʃ]、[ts]、[dʒ]、[dz] の間で自由変異する ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-affricate-c-varies-freely-among-t-ts⟧。アイヌ語の破擦音 *c* の調音点は日本語の「チュ」の子音よりもやや前寄りであるが、日本語の「ツ」ほど前寄りではないとされる ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-articulation-point-of-the-ainu-affricate-c⟧。

text.en: All eleven consonants can occur in syllable-initial position ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--all-11-consonants-can-occur-in-syllable-initial⟧. Syllable-initial stop consonants in Ainu are frequently voiceless sounds without noticeable aspiration, though rarely completely unaspirated ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-initial-stop-consonants-in-ainu-are-frequently⟧. Initial /c-/ is standardly realized as the voiceless palato-alveolar affricate [tʃ] ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--initial-c-is-standardly-realized-as-the-voiceless⟧. In southern Hokkaido Ainu, /c/ is realized as a voiceless alveolar affricate [tʃ] or, in the speech of some speakers, as [ts] ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-phoneme-c-is-realized-as-a-voiceless⟧. The affricate *ch* is realized as *ts*, *dz*, or *j* in careless speech, but is consistently *ch* in normal speech ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-affricate-ch-is-realized-as-ts-dz⟧. The letter *c* represents a single sound identical to the initial sound in Japanese *cha* ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-letter-c-represents-a-single-sound-identical⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the affricate /c-/ is a dental plosive fricative [tʃ, (ts)] and is not found as a final ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--affricate-c-is-a-dental-plosive-fricative-t⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, /c/ is an affricate [tʃ], and the syllables /ca, ci, cu, ce, co/ are pronounced almost identically to Japanese *cha*, *chi*, *chu*, *che*, *cho* ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--c-is-an-affricate-t-and-the-syllables⟧. Initial /h-/ assimilates its place of articulation to the following vowel: [h] before /a, e, o/, [ç] before /i/, and [ɸ] before /u/, though it can also be articulated further back near [h] before /u/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--initial-h-assimilates-its-place-of-articulation-to⟧. Weak fricative /h-/ in Hokkaido Ainu often becomes [ɸ] before /-u/ and does not appear as a final ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--weak-fricative-h-often-becomes-before-u-and⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, /y/ and /t/ cannot appear preceding /i/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-y-and-t-cannot-appear⟧, and /w/ cannot precede /u/ or /i/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-w-cannot-precede-u-or⟧. Morpheme-final /t/ alternates to [tʃ] before a suffix beginning in /i/ by the rule /t/ → [tʃ] / _i, as in [mat] 'wife' becoming [a-matʃi] 'my wife' ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--morpheme-final-t-alternates-to-t-before-a⟧.
text.ja: 11個の子音のすべてが音節頭に生起できる ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--all-11-consonants-can-occur-in-syllable-initial⟧。アイヌ語の音節頭の閉鎖音は帯気性の著しくない無声音であることが多いが、完全に無気音となることは稀である ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-initial-stop-consonants-in-ainu-are-frequently⟧。音節頭の /c-/ は無声後部歯茎破擦音 [tʃ] として実現するのが標準的である ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--initial-c-is-standardly-realized-as-the-voiceless⟧。南北海道アイヌ語において、音素 /c/ は無声歯茎破擦音 [tʃ]、あるいは一部の話者の発話では [ts] として実現する ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-phoneme-c-is-realized-as-a-voiceless⟧。破擦音 *ch* はぞんざいな発音では *ts*、*dz*、*j* などに響くが、通常の発音では常に *ch* である ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-affricate-ch-is-realized-as-ts-dz⟧。文字 *c* は日本語の「茶」の頭の音と同じ単一の音を表す ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-letter-c-represents-a-single-sound-identical⟧。北海道アイヌ語において、破擦音 /c-/ は歯破裂摩擦音 [tʃ, (ts)] であり、末尾には現れない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--affricate-c-is-a-dental-plosive-fricative-t⟧。樺太アイヌ語では /c/ は破擦音 [tʃ] であり、/ca, ci, cu, ce, co/ は日本語の「チャ、チ、チュ、チェ、チョ」とほぼ同じ発音である ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--c-is-an-affricate-t-and-the-syllables⟧。音節頭の /h-/ は後続母音により調音点が変わり、/a, e, o/ の前では [h]、/i/ の前では [ç]、/u/ の前では [ɸ] となることが多いが、/u/ の前でも [h] に近い音で発音される場合もある ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--initial-h-assimilates-its-place-of-articulation-to⟧。北海道アイヌ語において、弱い摩擦音 /h-/ は /-u/ の前でしばしば [ɸ] となり、末尾には現れない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--weak-fricative-h-often-becomes-before-u-and⟧。北海道アイヌ語では、/y/ と /t/ は /i/ の前に現れることができず ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-y-and-t-cannot-appear⟧、/w/ は /u/ および /i/ の前に現れることができない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-w-cannot-precede-u-or⟧。形態素末の /t/ は、/i/ で始まる接辞が付加される際に規則 /t/ → [tʃ] / _i により [tʃ] へ交替し、例として [mat]「妻」に対する [a-matʃi]「私の妻」がある ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--morpheme-final-t-alternates-to-t-before-a⟧。

text.en: In syllable-coda position, the release of consonants is not prominent, and stops in particular lack plosion ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-transition-release-of-syllable-coda-consonants-is⟧. Syllable-final stops /p, t, k/ are described as unreleased stops ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--coda-stops-unreleased⟧, realized in southern Hokkaido as unreleased [p̚], [t̚], and [k̚] as opposed to regular stops in onset position ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-stops-p-t-and-k-are-realized⟧, and in Hokkaido Ainu generally as unreleased and difficult to hear ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-syllable-final-stops-p-t⟧; Refsing, however, describes syllable-final /p, t, k/ in Hokkaido Ainu as weak plosives ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--coda-stops-weak-plosives-refsing⟧. The affricate /c/ is not found in syllable-final position ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-affricate-c-is-not-found-in-syllable⟧, and Hokkaido Ainu excludes both /c/ and /h/ from syllable-final position ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-c-and-h-cannot-appear⟧. Syllable-coda /-s/ is realized as palatalized [sʲ] after /a, u, e, o/, but as alveolo-palatal [ɕ] after /i/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--coda-s-is-realized-as-palatalized-s-after⟧. Ainu clearly distinguishes between the open syllable /si/ and syllable-coda /-s/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--ainu-clearly-distinguishes-between-the-open-syllable-si⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, plosives /p, t, k/ occur only in syllable onset and never in syllable coda ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-plosives-p-t-k⟧, and historical voiceless plosives all appear syllable-finally as /-h/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-finally-in-sakhalin-ainu-historical-voiceless-plosives⟧. Except for the Taraika dialect, the syllable-final stops /p/, /t/, /k/ and the tap /r/ have neutralized into /h/ in Sakhalin Ainu ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-except-for-the-taraika-dialect⟧. Sakhalin Ainu has the same consonant phonemes as Hokkaido Ainu, but /p, t, k, r, c/ cannot occur in final position ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--sakhalin-ainu-has-the-same-consonant-phonemes-as⟧. In syllable-final position in Karafuto dialects, *p*, *t*, and *k* become *h* (or *s* after *i*), *m* becomes *n*, and *r* becomes *rV* ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-syllable-final-position-in-karafuto-dialects-p⟧. Dialects on the northern east coast from Taraika to Nairo, and around Tarantomari on the central west coast, preserve syllable-final *p*, *t*, and *k* as in Hokkaido dialects ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-the-northern-east-coast-from-taraika-to⟧. The Esutoru dialect is reported to distinguish between syllable-final *-is* and *-ih* ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-esutoru-dialect-is-reported-to-distinguish-between⟧.
text.ja: 音節末の子音の出わたりは顕著ではなく、特に閉鎖音は破裂を伴わない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-transition-release-of-syllable-coda-consonants-is⟧。音節末閉鎖音 /p, t, k/ は内破音（無開放閉鎖音）として実現するとされ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--coda-stops-unreleased⟧、南北海道アイヌ語では音節頭の通常の閉鎖音に対し音節末では無開放の [p̚]、[t̚]、[k̚] となり ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-stops-p-t-and-k-are-realized⟧、北海道アイヌ語において一般に聞き取り難い内破音とされる一方、Refsingは北海道アイヌ語の音節末 /p, t, k/ を弱い破裂音と記述している ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--coda-stops-weak-plosives-refsing⟧⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-syllable-final-stops-p-t⟧。破擦音 /c/ は音節末には見られず ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-affricate-c-is-not-found-in-syllable⟧、北海道アイヌ語において /c/ と /h/ は音節末に現れることができない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-c-and-h-cannot-appear⟧。音節末の /-s/ は先行母音によって音価が変わり、/a, u, e, o/ の後ろでは口蓋化した [sʲ]、/i/ の後ろでは歯茎硬口蓋音 [ɕ] で発音される ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--coda-s-is-realized-as-palatalized-s-after⟧。開音節 /si/ と音節末の /-s/ ははっきりと区別される ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--ainu-clearly-distinguishes-between-the-open-syllable-si⟧。樺太アイヌ語では破裂音 /p, t, k/ は音節頭にのみ生起して音節末に来ることはなく ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-plosives-p-t-k⟧、歴史的な無声破裂音は音節末ではすべて /-h/ となって現れる ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-finally-in-sakhalin-ainu-historical-voiceless-plosives⟧。多来加方言を除き、樺太アイヌ語では音節末閉鎖音 /p/、/t/、/k/ および弾き音 /r/ が /h/ へと中和している ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-except-for-the-taraika-dialect⟧。樺太アイヌ語は北海道アイヌ語と同じ子音音素を持つが、/p, t, k, r, c/ は末尾に立つことができない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--sakhalin-ainu-has-the-same-consonant-phonemes-as⟧。樺太方言の音節末において、*p*、*t*、*k* は *h*（*i* の後では *s*）に、*m* は *n* に、*r* は *rV* に変化する ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-syllable-final-position-in-karafuto-dialects-p⟧。東海岸北部の多来加から内路にかけて、および西海岸中部の多蘭泊周辺の方言では、北海道方言のように音節末の *p*、*t*、*k* が保持されている ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-the-northern-east-coast-from-taraika-to⟧。恵須取方言は音節末の *-is* と *-ih* を区別すると報告されている ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-esutoru-dialect-is-reported-to-distinguish-between⟧。

text.en: Syllable-final /-m/ is a bilabial nasal [m] produced by closing both lips ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-final-m-is-a-bilabial-nasal-m⟧, while syllable-final /-n/ is an apico-dental nasal [n] pronounced with the tip of the tongue touching the back of the teeth ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-final-n-is-an-apico-dental-nasal⟧. In southern Hokkaido Ainu, the nasals /m/ and /n/ are realized as velar [ŋ] before the stop /k/, and as bilabial [m] and alveolar [n] in all other environments ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-nasals-m-and-n-are-realized-as⟧. The nasal *n* slightly palatalizes before *i* and becomes [ŋ] before *k*, but neither variant is an independent phoneme ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-nasal-n-slightly-palatalizes-before-i-and⟧. Syllable-final /-n/ assimilates to [m] before the bilabial consonants /p/ and /m/, and to [ŋ] before the velar stop /k/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-final-n-assimilates-to-m-before-the⟧. Because /n/ is automatically pronounced as [m] before /m/, the pronunciation [mm] for *n*+*w* represents conditioned allophony rather than phonemic alternation ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-phoneme-n-is-automatically-pronounced-as-m⟧. In certain words, an alternation or sound change from *m* to *p* occurs ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-sound-change-or-alternation-m-p-occurs⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, the syllable-final consonant *-m* is realized and transcribed as *-n* when it sounds like *-n* depending on the phonetic environment ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-syllable-final-consonant-m-is-realized-and⟧. In the Raichishka dialect of Sakhalin, /m/ is pronounced [m] in syllable onset and weakens in syllable coda ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-the-raichishka-dialect-m-is-pronounced-m⟧.
text.ja: 音節末の /-m/ は両唇を閉じて出す両唇鼻音 [m] である ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-final-m-is-a-bilabial-nasal-m⟧。音節末の /-n/ は舌先を歯の裏に当てて発音される歯裏鼻音 [n] である ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-final-n-is-an-apico-dental-nasal⟧。南北海道アイヌ語において、鼻音 /m/ と /n/ は閉鎖音 /k/ の前では軟口蓋鼻音 [ŋ] として実現し、その他のすべての環境では両唇音 [m] および歯茎音 [n] として実現する ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-nasals-m-and-n-are-realized-as⟧。鼻音 *n* は *i* の前では幾分口蓋化し、*k* の前では [ŋ] となるが、いずれも独立の音素ではない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-nasal-n-slightly-palatalizes-before-i-and⟧。音節末の /-n/ は、両唇音 /p/、/m/ の前では [m] になり、軟口蓋閉鎖音 /k/ の前では [ŋ] に同化する ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-final-n-assimilates-to-m-before-the⟧。/m/ の前で /n/ は自動的に [m] と発音されるため、*n*+*w* に対する [mm] という発音は音素交替ではなく条件異音による発音のバリエーションである ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-phoneme-n-is-automatically-pronounced-as-m⟧。語によっては *m* から *p* への交替ないし変化が見られる ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-sound-change-or-alternation-m-p-occurs⟧。樺太アイヌ語において、音節末子音 *-m* は環境によって *-n* と聞こえるときには *-n* と表記される ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-syllable-final-consonant-m-is-realized-and⟧。樺太のライチシカ方言では、/m/ は音節頭では [m]、音節末では弱くなる ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-the-raichishka-dialect-m-is-pronounced-m⟧。

text.en: Ainu lacks a phonemic contrast between voiced and voiceless consonants ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--no-phonemic-voicing-contrast⟧, and stops in particular lack a phonemic voicing contrast ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--no-stop-voicing-contrast⟧. Voiceless stops *k, t, p* and their voiced counterparts *g, d, b* belong to the same phonemes and can be substituted without affecting word meaning, with pure pronunciation being voiceless in principle ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--voiceless-stops-k-t-p-and-their-voiced⟧. Labial stops in particular often become voiced ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-ainu-labial-stops-in-particular-often-become⟧, and the tendency for stops to be perceived as voiced is reported to follow the hierarchy /p/ > /t/ > /k/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-tendency-for-stops-to-be-perceived-as⟧. Men are reported to produce voiced allophones of stops more readily than women ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--male-speech-voicing-tendency⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, stops and affricates lack a phonemic contrast between voiced and voiceless, or between aspirated and unaspirated ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-stops-and-affricates-lack-a⟧. Plosives /p, t, k/ in Hokkaido Ainu may become voiced intervocalically or following nasals ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--hokkaido-stops-voiced-intervocalic-postnasal⟧. In southern Hokkaido, stops /p/, /t/, and /k/ are often, though not necessarily, realized as voiced [b], [d], and [g] in intervocalic position, after nasals /m, n/, or after the tap /r/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-stops-p-t-and-k-are-often⟧, while /c/ is realized as a voiced affricate [dʒ] after nasals /m, n/ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--after-nasals-m-n-c-is-realized-as⟧. Stops and affricates in Hokkaido Ainu are voiceless word-initially and tend to be voiced intervocalically, especially immediately following a nasal ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-stops-and-affricates-are-voiceless⟧. In the Bihoro idiolect of Ginosuke Kikuchi, the voiced retroflex plosive [ɖ] was attested ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-the-bihoro-dialect-idiolect-of-ginosuke-kikuchi⟧. Hokkaido fricatives are only voiceless and never voiced ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-fricatives-are-only-voiceless-and⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, stops and affricates lack a phonemic contrast between voiced and voiceless or between aspirated and unaspirated, being generally voiceless and unaspirated ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-stops-and-affricates-lack-a⟧; they are voiceless word-initially and may be voiced intervocalically or immediately following a nasal ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-stops-and-affricates-are-voiceless⟧. Sakhalin fricatives are only voiceless and never voiced ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-fricatives-are-only-voiceless-and⟧. In the speech of Haru Fujiyama and Take Asai, voiced pronunciations of plosives were virtually absent, except for intervocalic /p/ occasionally being semi-voiced, whereas Maoka speaker Yuku Ota sometimes voiced them ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-the-speech-of-haru-fujiyama-and-take⟧. In Kuril Ainu, stops and affricates appear to lack phonemic oppositions between voiced and voiceless, or between aspirated and unaspirated ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-kuril-ainu-stops-and-affricates-appear-to⟧; they tend to be voiceless word-initially and voiced intervocalically ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-kuril-ainu-stops-and-affricates-tend-to⟧. Kuril fricatives appear to have been voiceless only and did not undergo voicing ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-kuril-ainu-fricatives-appear-to-have-been⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語には有声子音と無声子音の音素的対立が存在せず ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--no-phonemic-voicing-contrast⟧、閉鎖音にも有声・無声の音韻的対立は存在しない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--no-stop-voicing-contrast⟧。無声閉鎖音 *k, t, p* と対応する有声音 *g, d, b* は同一の音素に属し、置換しても語義に影響はなく、純正な発音ではすべての閉鎖音は無声であることを原則とする ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--voiceless-stops-k-t-p-and-their-voiced⟧。アイヌ語では特に唇閉鎖音は有声音になることも多く ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-ainu-labial-stops-in-particular-often-become⟧、破裂音が有声音に聞こえる度合いは /p/ > /t/ > /k/ であると言われている ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-tendency-for-stops-to-be-perceived-as⟧。男性は女性よりも破裂音を有声音として発音する傾向が強いと報告されている ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--male-speech-voicing-tendency⟧。北海道アイヌ語において、破裂音と破擦音は有声／無声、有気／無気の音韻的対立がない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-stops-and-affricates-lack-a⟧。北海道アイヌ語の破裂音 /p, t, k/ は母音間または鼻音の後で有声化することがある ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--hokkaido-stops-voiced-intervocalic-postnasal⟧。南北海道アイヌ語では、閉鎖音 /p/、/t/、/k/ は母音間、鼻音 /m, n/ の後、あるいは弾き音 /r/ の後において、しばしば（必然的ではなく）有声音 [b]、[d]、[g] として実現し ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--the-stops-p-t-and-k-are-often⟧、/c/ は鼻音 /m, n/ の後で有声破擦音 [dʒ] として実現する ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--after-nasals-m-n-c-is-realized-as⟧。北海道アイヌ語の破裂音・破擦音は語頭では無声、母音間では有声化しがちであり、特に鼻音の直後では有声化する ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-stops-and-affricates-are-voiceless⟧。美幌方言の菊池銀之助の話者個人語において、有声そり舌破裂音 [ɖ] が聞かれた ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-the-bihoro-dialect-idiolect-of-ginosuke-kikuchi⟧。北海道アイヌ語において、摩擦音は無声のみで有声化しない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-hokkaido-ainu-fricatives-are-only-voiceless-and⟧。樺太アイヌ語において、破裂音と破擦音は有声／無声、有気／無気の対立がなく、一般に無声無気であり ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-stops-and-affricates-lack-a⟧、語頭では無声であり、母音間や鼻音の直後では有声化することがある ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-stops-and-affricates-are-voiceless⟧。樺太アイヌ語の摩擦音は無声のみで有声化しない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-fricatives-are-only-voiceless-and⟧。藤山ハルと浅井タケの語りでは母音間の /p/ がたまに半有声になる以外は有声の発音はほとんど聞かれなかったが、マオカ方言話者の太田ユクは破裂音を有声化させることがあった ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-the-speech-of-haru-fujiyama-and-take⟧。千島アイヌ語において、破裂音と破擦音には有声／無声、有気／無気の音韻的対立がないと見られ ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-kuril-ainu-stops-and-affricates-appear-to⟧、語頭では無声、母音間では有声化する傾向にある ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-kuril-ainu-stops-and-affricates-tend-to⟧。千島アイヌ語の摩擦音は無声のみで有声化しなかったと見られる ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-kuril-ainu-fricatives-appear-to-have-been⟧。

text.en: In syllable-initial position, /r-/ is basically a tap [ɾ], but depending on the speaker it can be a trill [r] or a voiced stop close to [d] ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-syllable-initial-position-r-is-basically-a⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, initial /r-/ is retroflex [ʈ], and distinguishing it from [t] can sometimes be difficult ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-initial-r-is-retroflex-and⟧. Syllable-final /-r/ is lightly accompanied by the timbre of the vowel of the preceding or following syllable, sometimes making it difficult to distinguish from an /rV/ sequence ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-final-r-is-lightly-accompanied-by-the⟧. In words like /pirka/ or /arki/ where a syllable with /i/ precedes or follows /-r/, the consonant tends to be heard as [pirĭka] or [arĭki]; /arki/ may also be heard as [arăki] or [arŭki], but /pirka/ is never heard as *[pirăka] ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-words-like-pirka-or-arki-where-a⟧.
text.ja: 音節頭の /r-/ は基本的に弾き音 [ɾ] であるが、話者によって震え音 [r] や、有声閉鎖音で [d] に近い発音になる場合もある ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-syllable-initial-position-r-is-basically-a⟧。樺太方言では音節頭の /r-/ はそり舌の [ʈ] とされ、[t] との区別が困難になる場合がある ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-initial-r-is-retroflex-and⟧。音節末の /-r/ は前後の音節の母音の音色を軽くともなった発音になり、/rV/ との区別が難しい場合がある ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--syllable-final-r-is-lightly-accompanied-by-the⟧。/pirka/ や /arki/ のように /i/ を持つ音節が前後に来ると [pirĭka] や [arĭki] のように聞こえる傾向があり、/arki/ が [arăki] や [arŭki] と聞こえることはあっても /pirka/ が *[pirăka] と聞こえることはない ⟦claim:phon/consonant-inventory--in-words-like-pirka-or-arki-where-a⟧。
